node_definition: MRCA(Romanian, Italian, French, Spanish, ...): Eastern Romance + Italo-Western Romance
event: Aurelian's withdrawal of Roman troops/administration from Dacia south of the Danube, 271 CE (Watson 1999)
bound_type: point (as published); better treated as max-leaning soft interval
suggested_distribution: Normal(mu=1679, sd=150) or Uniform(1450,1900) soft; Normal(mu=1679, sd=383) [Maurits2020 rule of thumb: 95% in 929-2429]
alt_values_other_studies: Serva&Petroni2008 calibrate Italian-French separation = 1600 y; Bouckaert2012 calibrate a different node (Latin+Romance, see IE-LATROM-01)
notes: Assumes Daco-Romanian continuity north of the Danube after 271 CE; the continuity vs. later-immigration debate means Eastern Romance may have separated from Balkan Latin later (6th-7th c.). Also Latin continued as a written koine long after 271, so the date is an event, not a measured split. Holman et al. use present=2000 CE and the midpoint of source ranges; values here shifted by -50 to 1950 basis.
source_original: Watson A. 1999. Aurelian and the Third Century (as cited in Holman2011)

node_definition: MRCA(Italo-Dalmatian, Western Romance: Italian, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Catalan...)
event: Deposition of Romulus Augustulus, 476 CE ('fall' of Western Roman Empire; Bury 1923)
suggested_distribution: Normal(mu=1474, sd=383) [Maurits2020 rule of thumb: 95% in 724-2224]
notes: Political event used as proxy for linguistic divergence; no direct linguistic evidence. Holman et al. themselves note Bury argued against 476 as a real break. Holman et al. use present=2000 CE and the midpoint of source ranges; values here shifted by -50 to 1950 basis.
source_original: Bury JB. 1923. History of the Later Roman Empire (as cited in Holman2011)

node_definition: MRCA(North Germanic, West Germanic) [Holman: Gothic not in ASJP comparison]

suggested_distribution: Normal(mu=2050, sd=383) [Maurits2020 rule of thumb: 95% in 1300-2800]
notes: Ethnic identification of Cimbri/Teutones as Germanic speakers is itself debated; the node in Holman is effectively Northwest Germanic (no Gothic). Holman et al. use present=2000 CE and the midpoint of source ranges; values here shifted by -50 to 1950 basis.
source_original: Pohl W. 2004. Die Germanen (as cited in Holman2011)

node_definition: MRCA(North Germanic, West Germanic incl. Old English, OHG, Old Norse)
event: Earliest North Germanic runic inscriptions, 3rd c. CE (Bouckaert SI as quoted by Maurits2020)
suggested_distribution: Per Maurits2020: an inscription in a daughter gives only a MIN bound on the parent split; use offset/one-sided e.g. min 1700 BP soft, no informative max
notes: Explicitly criticised by Maurits2020: an inscription in a descendant language cannot by itself narrowly date the parent's disintegration; the implied 30-300 yr gap is unstated.
source_original: Bouckaert2012 SI; critique in Maurits2020
